Subject: FintechCo — logging controls & redaction (post-call recap)

Hi Sofia / Rajiv,

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps on logging, retention, and PII/redaction controls we discussed: 

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: make sure FintechCo can meet regulatory/data-retention needs while retaining observability for ML inference debugging.
- Primary concerns: request/response logs that may contain PII, headers (trace IDs, cookies), retention windows, and where logs are stored (residency).

What Redwood can offer (summary):
- Request/response logging: Off by default for bodies; enabled per-customer with granular toggles.
- Header handling: We log select metadata (timestamp, path, status code, latency, trace_id) by default. Sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie) are never logged.
- Redaction options:
  - Ingest-time redaction: automatic regex & structured-field stripping (names, SSNs, PANs) before storage.
  - On-disk masking: tokenization/hashing of fields like email/phone if you prefer reversible hashes.
- Retention & residency:
  - Default retention: 90 days; configurable per-customer (30/90/365+).
  - Archival: optional push to your S3/GCS with your KMS; logs can remain in-region.
- Access & auditing: role-based access to logs, audit trails for who retrieved data.

Attachments: attaching a short "redwood_logging_controls.pdf" that summarizes the above and our SOC2 summary "SOC2-Summary.pdf".

Open questions / next steps for your team:
1) Which environments will you want to send full request/response bodies (prod/staging)?
2) Do you have specific regexes or data dictionaries we should incorporate for redaction?
3) Would you like us to share a sample logging config (YAML) and a 20-minute technical demo with your infra/security folks?

If it helps, I can loop in Dev (engineer) to answer the more detailed questions about trace IDs and header handling — copying Dev on this thread.

Proposed next step: technical session next week with your infra/security (30 min). What windows work for you?

Thanks,

Hi Sofia / Rajiv — looping in Dev from our engineering team to provide the config snippets and answers to your specific questions.

Short answers first, details below: 
- Trace IDs: we include trace_id by default as a 128-bit hex string in metadata. We can hash/partial-mask trace IDs (e.g., last 8 chars) at ingest.
- X-Forwarded-For / client IP: we support pseudonymization (salted hash) or full removal per route.
- PII in bodies: yes — ingest-time redaction supports both regex-based and schema-based (JSON path) scrubbing before write. You can also opt to disable body logging entirely for specific routes.
- Retention: configurable per-customer and per-log-stream. We support policy-based retention: 30d, 90d, 365d, or custom. Archives can be pushed to customer-managed S3 (in-region) with KMS encryption.

Example snippets (illustrative YAML):

# Enable structured logging without bodies
logging:
  enable_request_body: false
  structured: true

# Ingest-time regex redaction
redaction:
  enabled: true
  rules:
    - name: email
      pattern: "\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b"
      replacement: "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
    - name: ssn
      pattern: "\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b"
      replacement: "[REDACTED_SSN]"

# Archive to customer S3 with KMS
archive:
  enabled: true
  destination: s3://fintechco-logs-prod-logs
  kms_key_id: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345

Other points: 
- Headers logged by default: path, method, status, latency, trace_id, x-request-id (if present). Anything else is opt-in.
- Attachments: I re-attached the summary PDFs for reference.
- SOC2 artifacts: SOC2-Summary.pdf is a customer-facing summary; for full artifacts we'd do an NDA/secure share if required.
